title: Rohingya food aid funded only to April 2027, commissioner warns
excerpt: Most refugees now get $7 to $10 a month for food, and acute malnutrition among young children has reached 14.6%.

image.alt: A WFP mobile storage unit at Balukhali Rohingya camp in Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar
image.credit: Rocky Masum / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
Funding for food assistance to Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh is secured only until April 2027, Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner Mohammed Mizanur Rahman told The Daily Star, which reported on 13 November that most refugees now receive less than the former $12 a month for food. He warned that further cuts were possible if no new pledges arrive in the next two or three months.

What has changed

Since 1 April, the World Food Programme (WFP) has replaced a flat monthly food entitlement of $12 a person with three levels based on household make-up and vulnerability, under what it calls a Targeting and Prioritisation Exercise. WFP's Andrey Shirkov gave the newspaper the breakdown:

  • $12 a person: 33% of refugees.
  • $10 a person: 50%.
  • $7 a person: 17%.

WFP said the change was not caused by funding shortages. Its monitoring found 70% of surveyed households had acceptable food consumption, down from 73% in 2025, and it said diet quality remains a concern, especially for women and young children. In September, WFP warned that general food assistance could be interrupted from December 2026 without more funding, the newspaper reported.

Refugees told The Daily Star they now eat mostly rice and lentils. A woman who fled Myanmar in 2017 said her family of five receives $7 a person and can no longer buy vegetables.

Children's nutrition

The 2026 Nutrition SMART Survey, carried out by Action Against Hunger with UNICEF and WFP funding and presented on 28 October, found among Rohingya children:

  • Acute malnutrition: 14.6% of children aged 6 to 59 months, up from 8.6% in 2024 and 13.9% in 2025, according to UNHCR figures cited by the newspaper.
  • Stunting: 42.6%.
  • Underweight: 36.9%.
  • Minimum acceptable diet: only 37.3% of children aged 6 to 23 months.
  • No vegetables: 44.6% had eaten none the previous day.

The survey does not show whether the April changes contributed to the rise. UNICEF's 4 November humanitarian report said 10,400 Rohingya children with severe acute malnutrition were treated from January to September 2026, and 177,100 were screened for wasting.

UNHCR Bangladesh spokesperson Shari Nijman said the 2026 Joint Response Plan seeks $710.5 million for 1.56 million refugees and host community members, 26% less than the 2025 appeal.

Why it matters

Food assistance is the largest single item in the Rohingya response. With funding confirmed only to April and acute malnutrition among young children rising for a third year, nutrition, health and protection partners in the camps, many of them national NGOs, face higher caseloads on shrinking budgets. Donors deciding 2027 pledges in the coming weeks will set how far rations fall.

What to watch

New donor pledges to WFP before the end of the year, whether WFP confirms or lifts its warning of a December interruption, and planning for the 2027 Joint Response Plan.
